question: Is otopalatodigital syndrome type 1 inherited ?
references: This condition is inherited in an X-linked dominant pattern. The gene associated with this condition is located on the X chromosome, which is one of the two sex chromosomes. In females (who have two X chromosomes), a mutation in one of the two copies of the gene in each cell is sufficient to cause the disorder. In males (who have only one X chromosome), a mutation in the only copy of the gene in each cell causes the disorder. In most cases, males experience more severe symptoms of the disorder than females. A characteristic of X-linked inheritance is that fathers cannot pass X-linked traits to their sons.

Otopalatodigital syndrome type 1 (OPD1) is a rare genetic disorder. It is inherited in an X-linked dominant pattern. This means that the mutated gene responsible for the condition is located on the X chromosome. 

In females, who have two X chromosomes, a mutation in one of the X chromosomes is enough to cause the condition. Females with OPD1 are usually more severely affected than males, who have only one X chromosome. Males with OPD1 are typically more mildly affected, as they have only one X chromosome with the mutated gene.
